correctness.rationale: The proof is self-contained after one published existence theorem. Binary affine generator columns force minimized nontrivial recovery sets to have odd size at least three. Recovery triples translate exactly to nonzero point sets of two-dimensional subspaces. The Năstase--Sissokho theorem supplies \((2^m-5)/3\) disjoint triples for odd \(m\). Any putative additional disjoint recovery set would force a partial two-spread covering all but one nonzero vector; XOR summation rules that out. Adding the target singleton gives \(t_{\max}=(2^m-2)/3\).
